summary.headline: Vidya Wires H1 FY27 revenue rose 42.6% to Rs 11,306.5 mn and PAT to Rs 319.7 mn, with H1 EBITDA/kg at about Rs 59 as ALCU ramps up.
summary.overview: Consolidated Q2 FY27 revenue from operations was reported at Rs 5,809.4 mn, up 52.5% YoY and 5.68% QoQ, with H1 revenue of Rs 11,306.5 mn (up 42.63%). H1 EBITDA was Rs 491.8 mn against Rs 382.64 mn and PAT was Rs 319.7 mn against Rs 225.3 mn, with the figures including ALCU's first half of operations. Management said ALCU copper lines are running at a healthy share of capacity, aluminium volumes build from end-Q3, and CTC production starts by mid-December with revenue from Q4. Analysts pressed on volumes and per-tonne profitability; management did not disclose volume numbers or FY27/FY28 guidance figures.

financial_highlights.change: down QoQ from est. Rs 52,000-53,000/t in Q1

segments.name: ALCU (copper)
segments.commentary: Copper lines started production in February and are running at a healthy share of capacity with monthly output rising. ALCU contributed roughly Rs 60 Cr in Q1 and Rs 110 Cr in Q2 per analyst's calculation, about 18-20% of Q2 revenue.

segments.name: ALCU (aluminium)
segments.commentary: Lines are under testing and customers are approving products, with more approvals in process. Management expects aluminium volumes to build from the end of Q3 FY27.

segments.name: ALCU new products
segments.commentary: EV, round ripple and aluminium paper-covered wires are on regular customer orders. Lines are installed for aluminium enameled wires and strips, paper-covered aluminium strips, PV ribbon, and copper busbars and foils.

guidance_outlook: CTC (continuously transposed conductor) production to begin by mid-December 2026 (end of Q3), with revenue contribution from Q4 FY27; initial focus on mid-size power transformers before large HVDC transformers.
Management estimates 6-9 months to get empanelment for HVDC transformer supply.
ALCU capex expected to be largely complete by end of Q3 FY27; unspent IPO funds held in fixed deposits.
Management expects Q3 and Q4 to be seasonally better quarters with volume growth; said FY28 will be better than FY27 but declined to give volume numbers.
Management guided EBITDA per tonne to rise to around Rs 60-65/kg in the future, per CFO's response to an individual investor's question (not a formal guidance).
capex_capacity: ALCU added capacity: about 10,000-11,000 MT of the planned 18,000 MTPA installed so far; the balance is expected by mid-December or around January 2027, later than the earlier pre-Diwali target.
Installation and construction at ALCU expected to finish by December 2026.
CTC plant is close to complete; trial production by mid-December 2026.
Export shipments from ALCU started to Israel and Nepal; first shipment also to a US client for PV ribbon. Management targets exports at a quarter of revenue once expansion is complete.
demand_pricing: Management cited renewables order scenario as very bullish, with renewable installations recovering after a slowdown over the past 2-4 months due to transmission delays.
Data center orders for copper busbars have started; EV charging demand and general power/transformer demand cited as growth drivers.
Raw material (copper) price increases and Middle East issues cited as headwinds to margins, but volumes maintained at or above prior-year levels.
Q1 volumes were affected by war/Middle East scenario; Q2 volume improved, though analyst estimated Q2 volume at about 4,300-4,500 tonnes (not confirmed by management).
Management said ALCU products are being offered to existing Vidya Wires customers to widen the range supplied by one vendor.

qa_highlights.question: How should margins be read given ALCU's higher-margin mix; what are EBITDA and spends per kg?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said H1 FY27 EBITDA per kg is about Rs 59 versus about Rs 44 in H1 FY26, growth of roughly 34%. The analyst had cited Rs 47-48 exit for FY26.

qa_highlights.question: Is PV ribbon for domestic or export market?
qa_highlights.answer: MD said demand for PV ribbon is recovering with solar module growth; Vidya is seeking more domestic share and has started exports to a US client.

qa_highlights.question: Why was Q2 EBITDA per tonne lower than Q1 despite higher volume?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said fixed costs have kicked in while volumes have not grown fully, pressuring EBITDA; teething issues are expected to be resolved and coming quarters should be better.

qa_highlights.question: What is the CTC timeline and HVDC plans?
qa_highlights.answer: MD said CTC trial production by mid-December, starting with mid-size power transformers; HVDC supply would follow after performance is proven, with 6-9 months of empanelment expected.

qa_highlights.question: Will volume data be disclosed, and what is the FY27/FY28 volume outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: MD said volume data will be considered for future investor presentations given mixed products and two plants; he declined to give numeric FY27 or FY28 guidance, only saying FY28 will be better.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 18,000 MTPA ALCU capacity fully installed and on time?
qa_highlights.answer: MD said about 10,000-11,000 MT is installed, with the balance by mid-December or around January, slightly later than planned due to execution time.

qa_highlights.question: Status of the Rs 50 Cr tax notice?
qa_highlights.answer: MD said assessment is complete, the company has filed for the next stage, the demand has reduced to a small amount, and management expects it to come down to almost zero.

qa_highlights.question: Volume split between old and new facilities for Q1 and Q2?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to disclose volumes by facility, citing only that ALCU's contribution is about 4-5% on a percentage basis.

risks_watch: Aluminium volume ramp depends on converting customer approvals into regular orders from end-Q3 FY27.
CTC start by mid-December and revenue from Q4 FY27 depend on trial production and customer confidence; HVDC empanelment is 6-9 months away.
ALCU capacity completion slipped from pre-Diwali target; balance 7,000-8,000 MT expected by mid-December or January 2027.
EBITDA/tonne pressure from fixed costs on ALCU and copper price volatility; management has not given a numeric target beyond an informal Rs 60-65/kg.
Volume disclosure remains limited: no facility-wise or product-wise volume data; management committed to consider adding it to investor presentations.
Tax demand (about Rs 50 Cr notice) is in appeal; outcome not yet final.
summary.management_tone: Confident on ALCU's copper ramp, CTC timing and renewables demand, but cautious and evasive on volumes, FY28 numbers and capacity completion dates, which slipped from the earlier pre-Diwali target.
key_quotes: Within 8 months of starting production in February, the copper lines are already running at a healthy share of their capacity and output has risen each month.
The first shipments have gone to Israel and Nepal.
We expect CTC to start contributing to revenue from the fourth quarter.
Not disclose any volume numbers, but the volume here can say, on a percentage basis we are about 4% to 5%.

adds.what: ALCU copper wire capacity, about 10,000-11,000 MT of planned 18,000 MTPA installed so far
ALCU CTC (continuously transposed conductor) plant, trial production by mid-December 2026
ALCU aluminium lines, volumes build from end of Q3 FY27

growth.why: No numeric FY27 revenue guidance; management says Q3/Q4 seasonally better and FY28 better than FY27, backed by ALCU copper lines (10-11k of 18k MT installed), CTC production by mid-December with revenue from Q4, and aluminium volumes from end-Q3, though volumes were not quantified and the balance of capacity slipped to around January 2027.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: H1 FY27 EBITDA/kg at about Rs 59 vs Rs 44 in H1 FY26 (~34% up), but Q2 EBITDA/t fell to est. Rs 48,000-49,000 from Rs 52,000-53,000 in Q1 as fixed costs hit before volumes fully ramp; informal target Rs 60-65/kg is not formal guidance.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: ALCU copper has about 10,000-11,000 MT of the planned 18,000 MTPA installed, with the 7,000-8,000 MT balance due mid-December to January 2027, and CTC trial production by mid-December; the timeline has already slipped from pre-Diwali.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management expects Q3 and Q4 to be seasonally better with volume growth and FY28 better than FY27, but gave no numeric volume guidance; ALCU is about 18-20% of Q2 revenue per analyst estimate (management said 4-5% on a percentage basis, conflicting), and aluminium volumes only build from end-Q3.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Capex is expected to be largely complete by end-Q3 FY27 and the unspent IPO funds sit in fixed deposits, so a new capex plan is not signalled; with ALCU still ramping, utilisation is not disclosed to judge the need.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: No numeric FY27 or FY28 guidance was given, management declined volume numbers, and the Q2 per-tonne EBITDA dip points against an upgrade.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Capacity completion already slipped from pre-Diwali to January 2027, aluminium volumes depend on converting approvals from end-Q3, and copper price increases and Middle East issues are cited as margin headwinds.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: CTC production starts by mid-December with revenue from Q4 FY27, initially for mid-size power transformers, and aluminium enameled wires, PV ribbon and copper busbars are on regular orders or lines are installed; HVDC empanelment is 6-9 months away.

rows.label: ALCU exports (Israel, Nepal, US PV ribbon client)
rows.why: Exports from ALCU have started to Israel and Nepal plus a first US PV ribbon shipment, and management targets exports at a quarter of revenue once expansion is complete (current contribution not disclosed).

rows.label: Renewables and data-centre demand
rows.why: Management calls the renewables order scenario very bullish after a 2-4 month slowdown from transmission delays, and copper busbar orders for data centres have started.

rows.label: Rs 50 Cr tax demand resolution
rows.why: Assessment is complete and the demand has fallen to a small amount that management expects to reach almost zero, but the matter is still in appeal with no final outcome.

tone.note: Management was confident on the copper ramp, CTC timing and renewables demand but cautious on volume disclosure, FY28 numbers and the slipped capacity completion date; analysts pressed on volumes and per-tonne profitability, which fell QoQ.
